ideas.source: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2004), 'Power and Bipower Variation with Stochastic Volatility and Jumps', Journal of Financial Econometrics 2(1), 1-37; and (2006), 'Econometrics of Testing for Jumps in Financial Economics Using Bipower Variation', Journal of Financial Econometrics 4(1), 1-30. Overview: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/5213484_Econometrics_of_Testing_for_Jumps_in_Financial_Economics_Using_Bipower_Variation ; threshold-bipower refinement for finite-sample bias: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314836310_Threshold_Bipower_Variation_and_the_Impact_of_Jumps_on_Volatility_Forecasting

ideas.name: First-Half-Hour Sets the Last-Half-Hour
ideas.entry_rule: At 15:30:00 ET compute r1 = (close of the 09:30-10:00 30-minute bar / previous session's official 16:00 close) - 1. If r1 > +0.05% enter long at the 15:30 bar open; if r1 < -0.05% enter short at the 15:30 bar open; otherwise no trade. Optional gate: only trade when the session's realized variance (sum of squared 5-min returns from 09:30 to 15:30) is above its own 20-session median, and when cumulative session volume to 15:30 is above its 20-session median.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the official 16:00 close of the same session, unconditionally. Never hold overnight. Optional hard stop at 1.0x the median 30-minute range for the 15:30-16:00 slot over the last 20 sessions.
params: signal window (15/30/60 min from the open)
use r12 (15:00-15:30 return) as an additional or alternative signal
ideas.why: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou attribute it to late-day rebalancing by intraday traders and to infrequent-rebalancing investors (leveraged ETFs, target-vol funds) whose end-of-day trades are mechanically in the same direction as the day's early move. The first half-hour aggregates overnight information; the last half-hour is when the flow that must respond to it actually executes. Predictability is stronger on high-volatility, high-volume, recession and macro-release days, which is what a flow story predicts.
ideas.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, "Market intraday momentum," Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 2018, 394-414 (working paper: SSRN id 2440866); replication summary at alphaarchitect.com/attention-prop-traders-the-first-half-hour-of-trading-predicts-the-last-half-hour/
ideas.novelty: Direction comes from a clock-anchored return over a fixed calendar window, not from any moving average, oscillator or breakout level. The holding period is a fixed 30-minute slot at the end of the session - the position is defined by the clock, not by price behaviour.

ideas.name: Selloff-Into-The-Close Overnight Reversal
ideas.entry_rule: At 15:58 ET compute the last-hour return L = (last trade price / close of the 15:00 bar) - 1 and sigma_L = the standard deviation of L over the previous 60 sessions. If L < -0.75 x sigma_L, buy at the official 16:00 close. Do not take the mirror short when L > +0.75 x sigma_L - the effect is asymmetric.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the next session's 09:30 open. Variant: hold to 10:00 ET and exit at the 10:00 bar close. Skip the trade entirely if the session is the last before a market holiday closure of more than one calendar day.
inputs: 1-min or 5-min intraday bars for the 15:00-16:00 window
params: add a market-wide filter (only when SPY also sold off into the close)
ideas.why: Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan show that essentially the entire US equity premium accrues in a narrow overnight window coinciding with the European open, and that it is strongly predicted by end-of-day order imbalance in the preceding US session, asymmetrically: market selloffs generate robust positive overnight reversals while rallies produce much weaker ones. The mechanism is Grossman-Miller inventory: dealers absorbing the close-of-day sell imbalance demand compensation and unwind at the first deep liquidity, which for US equities is the European morning. Since a 2-3am ET bar does not exist for US equities, the tradable version conditions on the imbalance proxy at the close and captures the reversal in the close-to-open return.
ideas.source: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan, "The Overnight Drift," Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 917 / CEPR DP14462; published version in Review of Financial Studies
ideas.novelty: Signed late-session return used as an order-imbalance proxy, and the position is held only across the non-trading hours. Deliberately one-sided - the paper's asymmetry means adding the short leg should degrade it, which is itself a falsifiable test.

ideas.name: Closing Auction Deviation Fade
ideas.timeframe: 1-minute bars for the signal, close-to-open holding
ideas.entry_rule: Let P_1559 = close of the 15:59 one-minute regular-hours bar and P_close = the official daily closing price (the 16:00 auction print). Compute d = P_close/P_1559 - 1. Compute q = the 80th percentile of |d| over the previous 60 sessions. Require auction participation: volume in the 15:59 bar plus the closing print > 2x the 20-session median for that slot. If d > +q, short at the closing price; if d < -q, buy at the closing price.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the next session's 09:30 open. Stop: exit at 09:31 regardless if the open gaps further than 2x |d| in the adverse direction. Variant: exit half at the open and half at 10:00.
inputs: official daily close and closing volume
params: restrict to month-end, quarter-end and index-rebalance dates where the effect is largest
exit at open vs half-life scaling
minimum deviation floor in basis points to cover the spread
ideas.why: Bogousslavsky and Muravyev show closing auction volume roughly doubled as a share of daily volume over the 2010s, driven by ETF and index-fund ownership, that closing prices systematically deviate from pre-auction quote midpoints, and that these deviations revert by about half shortly after the close and fully overnight. The pressure is non-informational: passive funds must print at the official close for tracking-error reasons regardless of price, so the deviation is a liquidity premium paid to whoever supplies the other side, and it is repaid at the next open.
ideas.source: Bogousslavsky & Muravyev, "Who trades at the close? Implications for price discovery and liquidity," Journal of Financial Markets, 2023 (working paper version: static1.squarespace.com/static/6310c0b9bb63a25599f4418c/t/634ffc92f81e226b2c30654f/1666186387645/who-trades-at-the-close_June2021.pdf); State Street Global Advisors, "Closing time: How passive investing is reshaping equity market microstructure"
ideas.novelty: The signal is the discontinuity between the last continuous-session print and the auction print - a quantity invisible on any chart of bar closes, since most data pipelines treat the auction price as simply the last bar's close. Nothing in the existing 32 looks at the auction versus continuous-session price at all.

ideas.name: Turn-Of-Month Cash Cycle Window
ideas.entry_rule: Let T be the last trading day of the calendar month, indexed from the exchange session calendar. Enter long at the 16:00 close of trading day T-4 (the fifth-to-last session of the month). Optional short leg: after the long leg is closed, enter short at the close of the 3rd trading day of the new month.
ideas.exit_rule: Close the long at the 16:00 close of the 3rd trading day of the following month. Close the short leg (if used) at the close of the 8th trading day of that month. No intra-window stops - the trade is defined purely by the calendar; use position sizing rather than stops to bound risk.
inputs: exchange session calendar to index trading days within each month
params: whether to include the mid-month short leg
scale exposure by the trailing 20-day realized volatility
skip December/January if the turn-of-year effect is traded separately
ideas.why: Ogden's payment-standardisation hypothesis: US wages, dividends, coupons and pension contributions cluster at the turn of the month, so new cash reaches the market on a fixed schedule. Etula, Rinne, Suominen and Vaittinen sharpen this with institutional flow data: funds must sell in the days before month-end to raise cash for month-end payments, depressing prices into T, and the pressure reverses once the cash is delivered - they document a return reversal following the last day of the month and estimate pension funds lose billions a year to the resulting round trip. The pre-T dip is the entry and the post-T reversal plus the new-money inflow is the payoff.
ideas.source: Ogden, "Turn-of-Month Evaluations of Liquid Profits and Stock Returns: A Common Explanation for the Monthly and January Effects," Journal of Finance 45(4), 1990, 1259-1272; Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, "Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs," Review of Financial Studies 33(1), 2020, 75-111
ideas.novelty: Entry and exit are both pure calendar indices with no price condition whatsoever - the only inputs are the session calendar and a position size. It has no indicator, no threshold and no chart pattern, which makes it orthogonal to every one of the 32 existing signals and usable as an overlay that gates them.

ideas.name: Strike Magnet Drift Into Expiration
ideas.entry_rule: On the Wednesday of expiration week, at the 15:55 bar, for every stock priced between $20 and $200 with 60-session median dollar volume above $50m, let K = the nearest multiple of $5 to the current price (sweep $2.50 for stocks under $50). Let g = (price - K)/K. If 0 < g <= +0.015, enter short. If -0.015 <= g < 0, enter long. Skip if |g| < 0.002 (already pinned) or if the stock's 20-day ATR/price exceeds 4% (too volatile to pin).
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the 15:45 bar on the third Friday, before the post-expiration unpinning. Stop out immediately if price moves further than 2.0% away from K in the adverse direction. Do not carry into the following Monday.
inputs: price level to infer the $5/$2.50 strike grid
exchange calendar for the third Friday
params: strike grid ($2.50 vs $5 vs $10 by price bucket)
ideas.why: Ni, Pearson and Poteshman document that on expiration dates, optionable stocks cluster at strike prices far more than chance allows, driven by hedge rebalancing by option market makers and by directional trading intended to move the price toward a strike. Between mid-week and Friday's close, the pinning force is a real order-flow gradient pointed at the nearest heavily-open-interest strike, which for most US equities sits on the $5 grid.
ideas.source: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman, "Stock price clustering on option expiration dates," Journal of Financial Economics 78(1), 2005, 49-87
ideas.novelty: The target price is derived from a fixed dollar grid rather than from any price history - a support/resistance level that exists because of contract specifications, not because of past trading. Round-number levels appear nowhere in the existing 32, and the effect switches on only in one week of each month.

ideas.name: Diurnal Relative Volume Thrust
ideas.entry_rule: For each 5-minute slot s of the session (09:30, 09:35, ..., 15:55), compute expected volume E_s = the median volume in slot s over the previous 20 sessions, and RVOL = current bar volume / E_s. Enter long at the next bar's open when: RVOL >= 3.0, the bar closes in the top 25% of its own high-low range, and the bar's close exceeds the highest high of the preceding 6 bars. Mirror for short. No entries before 09:45 or after 15:15.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the earlier of: 12 bars (60 minutes) elapsed; RVOL below 1.0 for 3 consecutive bars; a stop at the entry bar's opposite extreme; or 15:55 ET. Never hold overnight.
params: baseline statistic (median vs trimmed mean) and lookback (10/20/60 sessions)
ideas.why: Volume follows a pronounced and highly stable U-shape (Admati and Pfleiderer's concentrated-trading equilibrium; Andersen and Bollerslev's measurement of the diurnal factor). A flat 20-bar volume average is therefore dominated by the shape of the day, not by information: any 'volume surge' filter measured against a flat average fires almost exclusively in the first and last thirty minutes and is nearly blind at midday. Dividing by the slot's own historical median removes the seasonal factor, so the filter detects genuinely abnormal participation whenever it occurs - and abnormal participation at an unusual hour is a far stronger information signal than the same raw volume at 09:35.
ideas.source: Admati & Pfleiderer, "A Theory of Intraday Patterns: Volume and Price Variability," Review of Financial Studies 1(1), 1988; Andersen & Bollerslev, "Intraday periodicity and volatility persistence in financial markets," Journal of Empirical Finance 4(2-3), 1997, 115-158 (Fourier Flexible Form deseasonalization); synthesis of the two for a trading rule
ideas.novelty: The volume baseline is a time-of-day profile rather than a rolling average, which changes which bars fire, not just how often. This is categorically different from the existing 'Bollinger with volume', whose volume term is a flat moving average and therefore mostly re-expresses time of day.

ideas.name: Diurnal-Scaled Range Breakout
ideas.entry_rule: For each 5-minute slot s, compute D_s = the median (high - low) in slot s over the previous 20 sessions - a time-of-day-specific volatility unit. Enter long at the next bar's open when the current bar's close exceeds the highest high of the previous 12 bars by more than 0.25 x D_s. Mirror for short. Require the session to be between 09:45 and 15:30.
ideas.exit_rule: Initial stop at entry minus 1.0 x D_s(entry slot); profit target at entry plus 2.0 x D_s(entry slot); trailing stop that re-scales each bar to 1.0 x D_s(current slot), so the stop tightens automatically through the midday lull and widens again into the close. Time stop after 24 bars. Flat at 15:55.
params: lookback bars for the breakout level
recompute the diurnal table weekly vs daily
ideas.why: Andersen and Bollerslev show intraday volatility is the product of a strong deterministic diurnal factor and a persistent stochastic component, and that failing to separate them corrupts every volatility-conditioned inference. A conventional ATR is a blend of the two: an ATR computed on intraday bars is high simply because the sample straddles the open. Scaling both the trigger and the risk unit by the slot's own historical range means a 12-cent midday break and a 40-cent opening break are treated as equivalent events, and the stop distance stops being systematically too wide at lunch and too tight at the close.
ideas.source: Andersen & Bollerslev, "Intraday periodicity and volatility persistence in financial markets," Journal of Empirical Finance 4(2-3), 1997, 115-158; Andersen, Bollerslev, Dobrev & co-authors, "Time-Varying Periodicity in Intraday Volatility," CREATES RP 2018-05 (pure.au.dk/ws/files/120472862/rp18_05.pdf)
ideas.novelty: Both the entry threshold and the risk unit are functions of the clock, so the strategy's effective aggressiveness is constant in information terms across the session. The existing ATR expansion breakout uses a flat ATR and therefore concentrates its trades in the first hour by construction; this one deliberately does not.

ideas.name: Lunchtime Liquidity Vacuum Fade
ideas.entry_rule: Active only between 11:30 and 14:00 ET. For each 15-minute slot s in that window, compute M_s = the median absolute 15-minute return and V_s = the median volume, each over the previous 20 sessions. When a completed 15-minute bar has |return| >= 2.0 x M_s AND volume <= 1.0 x V_s - a large move on below-normal participation - enter at the open of the next 5-minute bar in the direction opposite to the bar.
ideas.exit_rule: Target: the close of the 15-minute bar immediately preceding the extending bar (a full retrace of the move). Stop: the extending bar's extreme plus 0.3 x M_s in price terms. Hard time exit at 14:00 ET regardless of P&L. One trade per symbol per session.
inputs: 20-session per-slot median absolute return and median volume
ideas.why: The U-shape means midday is the low point of both volume and volatility, so the marginal liquidity provider is thinnest there. A large midday move on below-normal volume is therefore near-definitionally a liquidity event rather than an information event: a single sizeable market order walking a thin book. Once it finishes, the book refills and the price reverts. The conditioning pair matters - the same size move on above-normal midday volume is the opposite signal, because abnormal midday participation is the strongest information tell of the session.
ideas.source: Synthesis. Built from the intraday U-shape literature (Admati & Pfleiderer 1988; Wood, McInish & Ord 1985; the lunchtime trough documented in Lund University master's essay 'The Intraday Dynamics of Stock Returns and Trading Volume', lup.lub.lu.se/student-papers/record/1973850) combined with the Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka finding that short-horizon reversal is driven by temporary liquidity imbalances lasting under an hour. No single paper states this rule; the conditioning on below-normal volume is my inference from the liquidity mechanism.
ideas.novelty: Fades a move because volume was LOW, inverting the usual confirmation logic, and only inside the one window of the day where thin books make that inference defensible. Distinct from VWAP z-score reversion and Keltner fade, both of which fire on distance from a level at any hour and take no view on participation.

ideas.name: Weekday-Normalized Gap Fill
ideas.entry_rule: At 09:35 ET compute the gap g = (today's 09:30 open / previous session's close) - 1. Compute sigma_w = the standard deviation of g over the last 26 occurrences of the SAME weekday (so Monday gaps, which span a weekend and often a three-day weekend, are scored against Monday gaps only). Let z = g / sigma_w. If z > 1.5 and the first 5-minute bar closes below its open, enter short at the 09:35 open. If z < -1.5 and the first 5-minute bar closes above its open, enter long.
ideas.exit_rule: Target: the previous session's close (complete gap fill). Stop: beyond the session extreme set in the first 5 minutes by 0.15 x daily ATR(14). Time exit at 12:00 ET if neither is hit. Flat by the close in all cases.
params: require the first-bar reversal confirmation or not
ideas.why: Overnight gap variance is structurally weekday-dependent: a Monday open follows roughly 65 hours of accumulated news while a Wednesday open follows 17.5, and the calendar adds three-day weekends and holiday closures on top. Pooling all gaps into one distribution means Monday gaps are systematically under-flagged and midweek gaps over-flagged. The literature also documents that overnight returns dominate intraday returns on every weekday but with distinct weekday profiles - Monday-to-Tuesday overnight consistently positive, Friday-to-Monday negative - so the sign and the dispersion both vary with the weekday.
ideas.source: Synthesis, built on the weekday-decomposition evidence: Birru, "Day of the week and the cross-section of returns," Journal of Financial Economics 130(1), 2018; CXO Advisory, "SPY by Day of the Week and Overnight" (1993-2017 decomposition); "Weekly Seasonality in Overnight Effects of the Stock Market," Applied Economics and Finance (redfame.com/journal/index.php/aef/article/download/7705/6965). The weekday-specific normalization is my construction, and the CXO analysis explicitly warns the weekday overnight edge is unstable across subperiods, so treat the z-scoring as the durable part and any weekday directional tilt as the fragile part.
ideas.novelty: The gap is scored against its own weekday's distribution rather than a pooled one, which changes which gaps qualify as extreme. The target is the prior close - a gap fill - which is a different exit structure from the opening range fade already in the set, and the entry needs no range to have formed.

ideas.name: Halloween Exposure Gate
ideas.entry_rule: Buy the index proxy or the strategy's normal long book at the 16:00 close of the last trading day of October. Treat this as an exposure gate rather than a standalone trade: during the November-April window run normal gross exposure, during May-October run reduced gross exposure (0% for the pure form, or 30-50% for a softened form).
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the 16:00 close of the last trading day of April. No stops. Softened variant: during the May-October flat period, remain in the market only during the turn-of-month windows defined in the Turn-Of-Month Cash Cycle idea, which is where much of the summer's positive return has historically been concentrated.
inputs: calendar month boundaries and exchange session calendar
params: window boundaries (31 Oct - 30 Apr vs 31 Oct - 31 May)
full flat vs partial exposure in summer
overlay the turn-of-month windows during summer
apply to index only vs to all strategy exposure
ideas.why: Bouman and Jacobsen documented significantly higher November-April returns than May-October returns in the large majority of the 37 markets they studied, a result that has held up in subsequent out-of-sample work more often than most calendar anomalies. Proposed causes are the seasonality of vacation-driven risk aversion and liquidity provision, and seasonal variation in the risk premium. As a standalone timing rule its Sharpe is modest; its practical value is as a gross-exposure gate over other strategies.
ideas.source: Bouman & Jacobsen, "The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle," American Economic Review 92(5), 2002, 1618-1635
ideas.novelty: This is the weakest idea in the batch and I am reporting it as an exposure overlay rather than a trade, because its standalone edge is small and it is the calendar anomaly most exposed to data-mining criticism. It is worth including only because it composes with the higher-frequency ideas above: gating turn-of-month, pre-holiday and intraday-momentum exposure by the six-month window is a cheap test of whether those effects themselves have a seasonal amplitude, which none of the underlying papers examine.

ideas.name: Naked POC Magnet
ideas.timeframe: intraday 1-5 minute, levels built from prior daily sessions
ideas.entry_rule: Build a per-session volume profile from 1-minute bars: price bins of width 0.05% of that session's open, each bar's volume spread evenly across the bins its [low, high] covers. POC = highest-volume bin's midpoint. Mark a session's POC 'naked' if no LATER session's [low, high] has ever contained that price. Maintain the list of naked POCs from the last 60 sessions. At every 5-minute bar close between 10:00 and 15:00 ET, with no open position: let U = nearest naked POC strictly above last price, D = nearest naked POC strictly below. Compute dU = (U - price)/ATR14_daily and dD = (price - D)/ATR14_daily. If 0.4 <= dU <= 2.0 and dU < dD, go LONG at market. If 0.4 <= dD <= 2.0 and dD < dU, go SHORT at market. Only one naked-POC trade per level per day.
ideas.exit_rule: Limit exit at the target naked POC price. Hard stop at 1.0 x ATR14_daily against entry. Force flat at 15:55 ET. Once price trades through it, the POC stops being naked and is removed from the list.
ideas.why: A POC is the price at which the largest quantity of contracts changed hands in a session, i.e. the price the most participants agreed on. When price leaves that level without ever retesting it, a large cohort of positions was opened there and never got a chance to be added to, scaled out of, or defended. Unfinished business at a heavily-traded price acts as a liquidity magnet: resting orders from that cohort sit near it, so price tends to be drawn back. This is a distribution-of-volume level, not a price-extreme level, which is why it does not coincide with Donchian/pivot/S-R levels.
ideas.novelty: Not an MA or oscillator at all. The level is derived from where volume was transacted (the mode of the volume-at-price histogram), and the tradeable condition is a topological one - the level has never been revisited - which no price-only indicator can express.
ideas.source: Market Profile / volume profile lineage (Steidlmayer, CBOT Liquidity Data Bank). Definitions and the naked/virgin POC concept per LuxAlgo concept library, https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/naked-poc/ and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/point-of-control/ ; profile construction per TradingView docs, https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000502040-volume-profile-indicators-basic-concepts/ . Exact bin widths, ATR gating and the 60-session horizon are my specification (the sources describe the concept, not testable thresholds).

ideas.name: Eighty Percent Rule Value Area Rotation
ideas.entry_rule: From the prior RTH session's 1-minute volume profile compute POC, then expand outward one bin at a time, always taking the higher-volume of the two adjacent bins, until 70% of session volume is enclosed; the enclosing range is [VAL, VAH]. Today: require the 09:30 ET open price to be OUTSIDE [VAL, VAH]. Then watch the 30-minute bars ending 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, ... If two CONSECUTIVE 30-minute bars both close inside [VAL, VAH], enter at the close of the second one, in the direction of travel across the value area: LONG if today's open was below VAL, SHORT if today's open was above VAH. One trade per day.
ideas.exit_rule: Target = the far edge of the value area (VAH if long, VAL if short). Stop = the near edge minus (for a long) 0.25 x (VAH - VAL), i.e. price re-exiting the value area on the side it came from. Force flat at 15:55 ET.
inputs: 1-minute OHLCV for the prior session (to build the profile)
params: stop buffer as fraction of VA width (0.1-0.5)
ideas.why: The value area is where 70% of the previous day's volume traded - the range the market collectively accepted as fair. Opening outside it and then being pulled back inside is evidence the overnight repricing was rejected. Once inside accepted value, there is no volume shelf to stop the auction until the opposite edge, so the market tends to rotate the full width. The two-period confirmation is what separates acceptance from a wick through the edge.
ideas.novelty: Entry is conditioned on a two-period acceptance test against a level defined by the volume distribution, and the target is structurally determined (opposite edge of the same distribution) rather than an ATR multiple or trailing stop. Nothing here uses a moving average, band, or oscillator.
ideas.source: The 80% rule as stated in market-profile literature - originating with Dalton, Jones & Dalton, 'Mind Over Markets'. Rule statement and value-area construction per https://marketprofile.info/articles/value-area-explained and the value-area statistics write-up at https://www.profitabul.com/learn/value-area-statistics . I pinned the ambiguous parts (which 30-minute periods count, the direction convention, the stop) to make it mechanical.

ideas.name: Value Area Overlap Regime Switch
ideas.entry_rule: Each session compute [VAL_t, VAH_t] (70% value area) from that session's 1-minute volume profile. Overlap ratio R_t = length([VAL_t,VAH_t] INTERSECT [VAL_{t-1},VAH_{t-1}]) / length([VAL_t,VAH_t] UNION [VAL_{t-1},VAH_{t-1}]); R_t = 0 if disjoint. BALANCE regime if R_t >= 0.60 AND R_{t-1} >= 0.60. MIGRATION-UP regime if R_t <= 0.20 AND POC_t > POC_{t-1}; MIGRATION-DOWN if R_t <= 0.20 AND POC_t < POC_{t-1}. Next session, after 10:00 ET: (a) in BALANCE, SHORT on the first 5-minute bar that closes above VAH_t, and LONG on the first 5-minute bar that closes below VAL_t; (b) in MIGRATION-UP, LONG on the first 5-minute bar that closes above VAH_t; (c) in MIGRATION-DOWN, SHORT on the first 5-minute bar that closes below VAL_t. If 0.20 < R_t < 0.60, take no trade that day.
ideas.exit_rule: BALANCE trades: target POC_t, stop 0.5 x ATR14(5-min) beyond the entry bar's extreme, flat at 15:55. MIGRATION trades: trailing stop at 1.5 x ATR14(5-min) from the best close since entry, no fixed target, flat at 15:55.
ideas.why: The same level - the edge of yesterday's value - means opposite things depending on whether the auction is rotating or discovering. Day-over-day overlap of the volume distribution is a direct measurement of which state you are in: heavily overlapping value areas mean both sides keep agreeing on the same prices (mean reversion at the edges), non-overlapping value areas mean the market is repricing and edge breaks continue. Most band-fade and breakout systems fail because they apply one mode unconditionally; the overlap ratio is the switch.
ideas.novelty: The regime detector is the geometric overlap of two volume distributions, not volatility (squeeze), not trend strength (ADX), not a moving-average relationship. The same trigger price produces a long or a short depending on that overlap, which no single-mode system does.
ideas.source: Auction-market-theory treatment of overlapping vs separated value areas, https://www.profitsmasher.com/2026/06/auction-market-theory.html and https://marketprofile.info/articles/value-area-explained (the sources say overlapping VAs = balance, separated = discovery, and prescribe fading vs following accordingly). The Jaccard-style overlap ratio and the numeric 0.60 / 0.20 cutoffs are my specification to make it computable.

ideas.name: Low Volume Node Traverse
ideas.timeframe: intraday 5-minute, profile built from 20 sessions of 1-minute bars
ideas.entry_rule: Build a composite volume profile from the last 20 sessions of 1-minute bars, bin width 0.10% of current price, restricted to [P - 3*ATR14_daily, P + 3*ATR14_daily]. Let m = mean volume across the non-empty bins in that window. An LVN is a maximal run of >= 3 consecutive bins each with volume < 0.30*m; an HVN is any bin with volume > 2.0*m. Rebuild nightly. Entry LONG: a 5-minute bar closes above the LOWER edge of an LVN run that sits above the previous close, the bar's close > its open, and the bar's volume >= 1.5 x the mean volume of the same bar-of-day slot over the prior 20 sessions. Entry SHORT: mirror - a 5-minute bar closes below the UPPER edge of an LVN run sitting below the previous close, close < open, same volume condition.
ideas.exit_rule: Target = the nearest HVN bin beyond the far edge of the LVN run (above for longs, below for shorts). Stop = 0.25 x ATR14_daily beyond the LVN edge you entered through, i.e. a re-entry into the prior high-volume region invalidates. Time exit if the far edge is not reached within 12 bars; force flat 15:55 ET.
params: LVN threshold as fraction of mean bin (0.2-0.4)
ideas.why: A low-volume node is a price range the market previously refused to transact in - it moved through fast because no one wanted to trade there. Those prices have no inventory to absorb an order, so when price re-enters an LVN it tends to traverse it quickly rather than consolidate; conversely, high-volume nodes are where inventory sits and price stalls. This gives a breakout whose target is structurally determined by the volume histogram, and a stop that is invalidated by the market accepting prices it previously rejected.
ideas.novelty: Not a price-extreme breakout: the trigger level and the target are both read off the volume-at-price distribution, so entries fire in the middle of a price range where a Donchian or ORB system sees nothing, and the profit target is the next volume shelf rather than a multiple of volatility.
ideas.source: LVN/HVN behaviour per https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/high-low-volume-nodes/ and the LVN strategy write-up at https://www.tradezella.com/strategies/low-volume-node ; the 'next HVN is the target, LVNs trade fast' target logic per https://ninjatrader.com/futures/blogs/how-to-trade-with-volume-profile-part-1/ . Numeric node thresholds and the RVOL trigger are my specification.

ideas.name: VPIN Toxicity Burst
ideas.entry_rule: Bucket 1-minute bars into equal-volume buckets of size V = (median daily volume over last 50 sessions) / 50; a bar that overfills a bucket is split pro rata. Within each bucket, for each 1-minute bar i: dP_i = close_i - close_{i-1}; sigma = stdev of 1-minute close-to-close changes over the trailing 250 bars; buyVol_i = vol_i * Phi(dP_i / sigma) with Phi the standard normal CDF (bulk volume classification); sellVol_i = vol_i - buyVol_i. For a completed bucket: signed imbalance S = (sum buyVol - sum sellVol)/V, in [-1, 1]. VPIN = mean of |S| over the last n = 50 completed buckets. Maintain the empirical percentile of VPIN over the trailing 1000 buckets. ENTRY: on the bucket at which VPIN crosses from below to above its 95th percentile, take a position in the direction of the sign of that bucket's S - LONG if S > 0, SHORT if S < 0 - at the open of the next 1-minute bar. No entries after 15:30 ET.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit when VPIN falls back below its 60th percentile, OR on a 1.5 x ATR14(5-min) adverse move, OR 60 minutes after entry, whichever first. Force flat 15:55 ET.
params: CDF choice: normal vs Student-t with 0.1-0.25 d.o.f.
ideas.why: VPIN measures order-flow toxicity: the fraction of volume that is one-sided, measured in volume time rather than clock time so that busy periods are stretched and quiet periods compressed. High toxicity means market makers are being adversely selected by informed traders; they widen and withdraw, and price moves in the direction of the toxic flow. Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara showed VPIN peaked hours ahead of the 2010 Flash Crash. Crucially, bulk volume classification was designed precisely so that the measure can be computed from bar aggregates without needing signed trades.
ideas.novelty: Sampling is by volume, not time, so the indicator has no fixed lookback in minutes at all - it adapts its own clock to activity. This is a fundamentally different information axis from any price-derived oscillator, and the imbalance is estimated by a probabilistic split of each bar's volume rather than the all-or-nothing sign that OBV uses.
ideas.source: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-Frequency World', Review of Financial Studies 25(5); and 'An Improved Version of the Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading', https://cfr.ivo-welch.org/published/papers/easley-prado-hara.pdf . BVC buy fraction = Phi(dP/sigma) and the 50-bucket rolling window confirmed against two open implementations: https://github.com/twowaymind/orderflow-metrics (functions bucketByVolume, bvcBuyFraction, vpin) and https://github.com/hanxixuana/flowrisk . The Student-t 0.25 d.o.f. variant is from their 2016 follow-up.

ideas.name: Volume Imbalance Bar Burst
ideas.entry_rule: Sign each 1-minute bar: b_i = +1 if close_i > close_{i-1}, -1 if close_i < close_{i-1}, and carry the previous sign if unchanged. Accumulate theta = sum(b_i * vol_i) from the start of the current event bar. Let E_T = EWMA (span 50) of the number of 1-minute bars consumed by completed event bars, and let v_plus = EWMA (span 50) of sum(vol_i where b_i=+1) per bar and v_minus likewise. Close the current event bar and start a new one when |theta| >= E_T * max(v_plus, v_minus). ENTRY: when an event bar completes having consumed T <= 0.30 * E_T source bars (an unusually fast, i.e. bursty, accumulation of one-sided volume), enter at the open of the next 1-minute bar in the direction of sign(theta). No entries in the first 10 minutes or after 15:30 ET.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit when the next event bar completes with theta of the opposite sign, OR at a stop of 1.0 x ATR14(5-min) against entry, OR at 3 completed event bars after entry, whichever first. Force flat 15:55 ET.
inputs: EWMA of bar durations and of signed volume
params: EWMA span for E_T and imbalance expectation (20-200)
burst threshold as fraction of E_T (0.2-0.5)
ideas.why: Time bars oversample dead periods and undersample bursts, so any signal computed on them mixes two regimes. Imbalance bars close when one-sided volume exceeds what the recent history leads you to expect - they sample when information arrives. The tradeable event is not the imbalance itself but the SPEED at which it accumulated: an imbalance bar that completes in a third of the usual number of minutes means a participant is taking liquidity urgently, which is the behavioural signature of a large order being worked aggressively rather than passively.
ideas.novelty: The entry condition is a property of the sampling clock (elapsed real time to fill an information quota), not a property of a price series. No indicator in the existing 32 has any concept of event-driven bar formation; every one of them reads a fixed-interval series.
ideas.source: Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' (Wiley, 2018), Chapter 2 - tick/volume/dollar bars and imbalance bars; the imbalance-bar threshold E_T * |2P[b=1]-1| construction. Open implementations: https://github.com/jzajpt/id-bars and the walkthrough at https://medium.com/data-science/information-driven-bars-for-financial-machine-learning-imbalance-bars-dda9233058f0 . I substituted the tick rule on 1-minute closes for true tick signs (the OHLCV-only proxy) and added the burst-speed entry, which is my own.

ideas.name: Time Of Day Relative Volume Z Thrust
ideas.entry_rule: Partition the RTH session into 78 five-minute slots. For slot s, compute mu_s = mean and sd_s = stdev of log(1 + volume) for slot s over the prior 20 sessions (skip half-days and days with a session-wide volume z above 4). For the current bar in slot s: z = (log(1+volume) - mu_s) / sd_s, and clv = (close - low)/(high - low) with clv = 0.5 if high == low. ENTRY LONG: z >= 2.0 AND clv >= 0.80 AND close > open AND close > the highest close of the prior 6 bars. ENTRY SHORT: z >= 2.0 AND clv <= 0.20 AND close < open AND close < the lowest close of the prior 6 bars. Enter at the next bar's open. Skip the 09:30 and 09:35 slots. No entries after 15:30 ET.
ideas.exit_rule: Target 2.0 x ATR14(5-min), stop 1.0 x ATR14(5-min), plus a time exit 12 bars after entry. Force flat 15:55 ET.
inputs: per-slot log-volume mean and stdev over 20 sessions
ideas.why: Intraday volume follows a strong U-shape - heavy at the open and close, thin at lunch - so a raw volume filter fires every morning and never at 13:00, which is exactly backwards. Normalising each bar against its own time-of-day distribution makes '3x normal' mean the same thing at 11:15 as at 09:45. A genuine participation shock at a time when nobody normally trades is much stronger evidence of new information than the same absolute volume at the open. Requiring the close near the bar extreme adds the direction: heavy volume with the close pinned at the high means the buyers absorbed everything offered.
ideas.novelty: The volume filter is a per-slot z-score of log volume against 20 sessions of the SAME clock slot, not a ratio to a trailing 20-bar average. Every 'volume > 1.5x average' rule in the existing set uses a trailing average that is contaminated by the U-shape and therefore measures time of day as much as it measures participation.
ideas.source: Time-of-day-normalised RVOL construction per StockCharts ChartSchool, https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/relative-volume-rvol , the same-time-of-day method described at https://stockbeep.com/blog/post/how-to-calculate-relative-volume-rvol-for-intraday-trading , and the intraday overlay at https://www.tradingview.com/script/fCgl6lLO-Intraday-RVOL-Overlay-Time-of-Day-Relative-Volume/ (all three explicitly flag the U-shape problem with flat averages). Log transform, z-scoring and the clv gate are my specification.

ideas.name: Session Volume Pace Divergence
ideas.category: effort vs result / cumulative relative volume
ideas.entry_rule: Define cumulative pace C(t) = (today's cumulative RTH volume through slot t) / (mean cumulative RTH volume through slot t over the prior 20 sessions). SHORT setup: let t1 be the slot of the session's high made at or before the current bar, established at least 6 bars ago; when a 5-minute bar at slot t2 > t1 prints a NEW session high, and C(t2) <= 0.85 * C(t1), enter SHORT at the close of the FIRST subsequent bar that closes below the low of the new-high bar. LONG setup: mirror with session lows and new session lows, C(t2) <= 0.85 * C(t1), entering on the first bar closing above the high of the new-low bar. Only fire after 10:30 ET; no entries after 15:15 ET. One trade per direction per session.
ideas.exit_rule: Target = session VWAP. Stop = 0.25 x ATR14(5-min) beyond the extreme of the new-high (or new-low) bar. Force flat 15:55 ET.
inputs: prior-20-session cumulative volume curve by slot
ideas.why: Wyckoff's law of effort versus result at session scale. If the market makes a higher high but the day's participation, measured against its own normal pace at that clock time, has DECAYED relative to where it was at the earlier high, then the extension is being made by fewer hands. That is the fingerprint of a move that has run out of the sponsorship that started it. Comparing pace at two specific times of day, rather than raw volume, removes the U-shape confound entirely.
ideas.novelty: The divergence is between price extremes and the session's cumulative participation pace - a path-dependent, time-normalised quantity - rather than between price and an oscillator. It also uses a structural target (session VWAP as the day's fair value) rather than a fixed multiple.
ideas.source: Synthesis. It combines the cumulative time-of-day RVOL definition from StockCharts ChartSchool RVOL and https://stockbeep.com/blog/post/how-to-calculate-relative-volume-rvol-for-intraday-trading with Wyckoff's third law (effort vs result) as set out at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/effort-vs-result/ . I am not aware of a published rule that compares cumulative pace at two intraday extremes; the construction and thresholds are mine.

ideas.name: Effort Result Regression Residual
ideas.timeframe: daily (also works on 5-minute with per-slot fitting)
ideas.entry_rule: Over a rolling window of the last 250 daily bars, fit OLS: |log(close_d / close_{d-1})| = a + b * log(volume_d) + e_d. Let sd_e be the residual standard deviation of that fit. For today's bar compute the residual r = actual |log return| - fitted. ENTRY when r <= -1.5 * sd_e (price moved far LESS than today's volume predicts) AND volume >= the 80th percentile of the last 250 days' volume AND the bar's range (high - low)/close >= the 50th percentile of the last 250 days (so it is a real bar, not a holiday). Direction from close location clv = (close - low)/(high - low): if clv >= 0.67, go LONG at the next open; if clv <= 0.33, go SHORT at the next open; otherwise no trade.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit at the close of the 5th trading day after entry, OR earlier at a 2.0 x ATR14 target or a 1.0 x ATR14 stop, whichever is hit first.
inputs: rolling 250-bar OLS of |log return| on log volume
ideas.why: Amihud's illiquidity ratio is |return|/volume - the price response per unit of trading. Fitting |return| on log volume estimates the same relationship but lets it be nonlinear in scale and gives you a well-defined 'expected move for this much volume'. A large NEGATIVE residual means enormous volume produced almost no price change: someone with size absorbed the entire flow at a fixed price. That is exactly Wyckoff's absorption, but expressed as a studentised residual so the threshold is comparable across symbols and volatility regimes. The absorber's side is inferred from where the bar closed within its range.
ideas.novelty: Turns 'high volume, small move' from an eyeball judgement into a residual from a fitted price-impact relationship, so the threshold self-calibrates to the symbol's own liquidity. No indicator in the existing 32 regresses price response on volume; the closest, ATR expansion, ignores volume entirely.
ideas.source: Synthesis, built on two cited pillars: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5, 31-56, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf , which establishes |return|/dollar-volume as the price response per unit of trading; and Wyckoff's effort-vs-result law as described at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/effort-vs-result/ . The OLS-residual formulation and the clv direction rule are my own.

ideas.name: High Volume Churn Bar Failure
ideas.entry_rule: Identify a CHURN bar: (a) its volume >= the 90th percentile of the same bar-of-day slot's volume over the prior 20 sessions; (b) its range (high - low) <= the 40th percentile of the last 100 bars' ranges; (c) its high equals the highest high of the last 20 bars, OR its low equals the lowest low of the last 20 bars. ENTRY: if the churn bar set the 20-bar HIGH, go SHORT on the first subsequent 5-minute bar that closes below the churn bar's LOW, provided that happens within 8 bars. If the churn bar set the 20-bar LOW, go LONG on the first subsequent bar that closes above the churn bar's HIGH within 8 bars. Cancel the setup if not triggered in 8 bars, or if a later churn bar replaces it.
ideas.exit_rule: Target = 1.5 x the churn bar's range, measured from the entry price. Stop = the churn bar's own extreme (its high for shorts, its low for longs). Force flat 15:55 ET.
params: target as multiple of churn range (1.0-3.0)
ideas.why: A bar that trades enormous volume at a swing extreme but goes nowhere is a fight that the initiator lost: the effort was expended, the result did not follow, so the incoming aggressive orders were fully met by resting size on the other side. The trade is not the churn bar itself - churn can precede continuation too - it is the subsequent FAILURE, when price closes back through the churn bar entirely. That confirms the absorbed side is now offside and must cover, which supplies the fuel for the move.
ideas.novelty: Distinct from the residual-regression version above in that it is a discrete bar taxonomy with a structural trigger and a stop defined by the churn bar's own geometry, and distinct from ATR expansion because it selects for range CONTRACTION on record volume - the exact opposite condition.
ideas.source: The 'High Volume Churn' bar type (high volume, low range) is one of the five classifications in the Better Volume indicator, documented at https://www.motivewave.com/studies/better_volume.htm and in the original description doc at https://c.mql5.com/forextsd/forum/147/better_volume_indicator__description.doc (the indicator originates from emini-watch.com). Those sources define the bar type and describe topping/bottoming sequences qualitatively; the percentile thresholds, the failure trigger and the exits are my specification.

ideas.name: No Demand No Supply Bar Fade
ideas.entry_rule: NO-DEMAND (short) setup, all conditions on bar t: close_t > close_{t-1}; range_t = high_t - low_t is LESS than range_{t-1} and LESS than range_{t-2}; volume_t is LESS than volume_{t-1} and LESS than volume_{t-2}; close_t is in the upper part of recent structure, i.e. (close_t - min(low, last 20 bars)) / (max(high, last 20) - min(low, last 20)) >= 0.60; and the market has been rising, i.e. close_t > close_{t-5}. Enter SHORT at the open of bar t+1. NO-SUPPLY (long) setup is the exact mirror: close_t < close_{t-1}, range_t below both prior ranges, volume_t below both prior volumes, position in 20-bar range <= 0.40, close_t < close_{t-5}. Enter LONG at the open of bar t+1.
ideas.exit_rule: Stop 1.0 x ATR14 beyond the signal bar's extreme (above its high for shorts). Target 2.0 x ATR14. Additional invalidation exit: close the trade immediately if any bar prints volume > 1.5 x the 20-bar mean volume with a close beyond the signal bar's extreme in the trade's adverse direction. Time exit after 8 bars.
inputs: prior two bars' range and volume
params: number of prior bars volume must undercut (2-3)
ideas.why: In Wyckoff/VSA terms, an up bar on shrinking spread and shrinking volume says the rally is unattended - professional money is not participating in the advance. The mark-up is being carried by residual retail bids with nothing behind them, so the path of least resistance is down. The two-bar volume comparison is the operative test: it is not 'low volume' in absolute terms, it is lower than each of the immediately preceding bars, which are the ones the same participants just traded.
ideas.novelty: A three-bar relational pattern in the volume series combined with narrowing spread and position within the swing - no averages, no oscillators, no thresholds on a smoothed series. It is also the rare volume signal that fires on a QUIET bar rather than a loud one, so it selects a completely different population of setups than any relative-volume rule.
ideas.source: Tom Williams' Volume Spread Analysis, derived from Wyckoff. Bar definitions per https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/no-demand-no-supply-bars/ (up bar, narrow spread, volume lower than each of the previous two bars) and the VSA overview at https://takeprofitapp.com/en/learn/volume-spread-analysis-vsa . The position-in-20-bar-range gate, the trend lookback, and all exits are my specification - the source rules are qualitative about context.

ideas.name: Stopping Volume Climax Reversal
ideas.entry_rule: CLIMAX-LOW (long) bar t: volume_t >= 3.0 x the mean volume of the prior 20 bars (intraday: 3.0 x the same-slot mean over 20 sessions); range_t >= 2.0 x ATR14 measured at t-1; low_t is the lowest low of the last 20 bars; and close_t is in the TOP 25% of its own range, (close_t - low_t)/(high_t - low_t) >= 0.75. ENTRY: a resting buy stop at high_t + 0.05 x range_t, valid for the next 5 bars only. CLIMAX-HIGH (short) bar t is the mirror: same volume and range conditions, high_t the highest high of the last 20 bars, close in the BOTTOM 25% of its range; resting sell stop at low_t - 0.05 x range_t, valid 5 bars.
ideas.exit_rule: Stop at low_t - 0.10 x range_t for longs (high_t + 0.10 x range_t for shorts) - i.e. beyond the climax extreme. Target = low_t + 3.0 x range_t for longs. Time exit 10 bars after fill. If the stop order is not filled within 5 bars, cancel it.
params: target as multiple of climax range (2-5)
ideas.why: Stopping volume is the moment a trend's supply is exhausted: enormous volume, a wide bar in the trend direction, but a close far back toward the opposite end. The sellers got their fills - into a bid large enough to absorb all of it and then push price back up within the same bar. The distinguishing feature versus ordinary high-volume selling is precisely that the close lands opposite the direction of travel. Requiring an actual break of the climax bar's high before entering avoids catching the many climaxes that simply keep going.
ideas.novelty: Selects for WIDE range on record volume with a reversed close - the exact inverse condition to the churn-bar idea above, and a different population of bars again from ATR expansion breakouts (which trade in the direction of the expansion, not against it). Entry is a stop order with a defined expiry, so the exit structure is also different.
ideas.source: Wyckoff selling/buying climax and VSA stopping volume as described at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/effort-vs-result/ and https://takeprofitapp.com/en/learn/volume-spread-analysis-vsa ('a high volume bar at the end of a trend where price barely progresses in the trend direction, with close opposite to trend'). The 3x volume / 2x ATR / top-quartile-close thresholds, the stop-entry mechanic and its 5-bar expiry are my specification.

ideas.name: Pocket Pivot Volume Signature
ideas.entry_rule: On day t, all of: (1) close_t > open_t AND close_t > close_{t-1}; (2) volume_t > the MAXIMUM volume of every DOWN-close day among days t-10 to t-1 (a down-close day is one where close < previous close); if there are no down days in that window, the condition fails; (3) close_t > SMA(close, 10); (4) SMA(close, 10) > SMA(close, 50); (5) close_t >= 0.80 x the highest close of the last 250 days (in the upper fifth of the annual range); (6) the day is not a gap-and-run: (high_t - low_t)/close_t <= 1.5 x the mean of that ratio over the prior 10 days. Buy at the close of day t.
ideas.exit_rule: Initial stop at min(low_t, low_{t-1}) - 0.25 x ATR14. After entry, exit on the first daily close below SMA(close, 10) that also has volume >= the 20-day mean volume. Hard profit target at +8% from entry, or trail with a 3.0 x ATR14 chandelier stop from the highest close since entry (whichever the parameter sweep prefers).
ideas.why: The comparison basis is the point. Comparing today's volume to the largest DOWN-day volume of the last two weeks asks a specific question: is today's buying larger than the largest recent selling? That fires inside a quiet consolidation, before the obvious breakout, because it does not require beating the up days. It is a supply-exhaustion test rather than a demand-surge test, so it catches the accumulation phase where the risk point (the base low) is close by.
ideas.novelty: The volume comparator is a conditional maximum over a subset of prior bars selected by their own price direction, not a mean or a percentile of all bars. Nothing in the existing 32 conditions a volume threshold on the sign of prior bars.
ideas.source: Gil Morales & Chris Kacher, 'Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple' (Wiley, 2010), chapter on pocket pivots and standard breakout buy points - https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/trade-like-an/9780470616536/9780470616536_pocket_pivots_and_standard_breakout_buy.html ; rule restatement ('volume must exceed the highest volume of any down day over the previous ten trading sessions') at https://www.tradingsim.com/blog/vdu-and-pocket-pivots and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/pocket-pivot/ . The annual-range floor, gap filter and exits are my specification.

ideas.name: Volume Dry Up Then Expansion
ideas.entry_rule: STAGE 1 - mark a VDU day d: volume_d < 0.50 x SMA(volume, 50) AND (high_d - low_d) <= the 40th percentile of the last 50 daily ranges AND close_d >= 0.85 x the highest close of the last 250 days AND close_d > SMA(close, 50). Record pivot = max(high over days d-4 .. d) and floor = low_d. STAGE 2 - entry: within the next 5 trading days, a day closes ABOVE pivot with volume >= 1.5 x SMA(volume, 50). Buy at that close. Cancel the setup if 5 days pass without the trigger, or if any close falls below floor.
ideas.exit_rule: Initial stop at floor - 0.25 x ATR14. Then trail with a 3.0 x ATR14 chandelier stop from the highest close since entry. Additional exit: a daily close below pivot on volume >= 1.5 x SMA(volume, 50) within the first 5 days after entry (failed breakout).
ideas.why: Volume drying up inside a consolidation near the highs means supply has been exhausted - the sellers who wanted out are out, and nobody is being forced to hit bids. That is a low-risk condition, but by itself it is not a signal, because dry-up can persist indefinitely. The signal is the transition: the first day that a demand surge (volume expansion) coincides with a break of the dry-up pivot. The two-stage structure means the stop sits at the dry-up low, which is both nearby and structurally meaningful.
ideas.novelty: A two-stage, state-machine entry with a bounded arming window, where stage 1 is a volume CONTRACTION test and stage 2 is a volume EXPANSION test. This is orthogonal to squeeze release and ATR expansion, which key off volatility contraction/expansion and never look at volume. It is also distinct from the pocket pivot, whose comparator is down-day volume rather than a moving average.
ideas.source: Volume Dry Up as used in the O'Neil/Minervini lineage; the operational definition 'the VDU candle must be less than 50% of the average volume' and the VDU-then-pocket-pivot sequencing are set out at https://www.tradingsim.com/blog/vdu-and-pocket-pivots , with the surrounding volatility-contraction context at https://www.tradingsim.com/blog/volatility-contraction-pattern . The arming window, pivot definition and exits are my specification.

ideas.name: Accumulation Distribution Regression Divergence
ideas.entry_rule: Maintain the Chaikin Accumulation/Distribution line: MFM_t = ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low), with MFM = 0 if high == low; ADL_t = ADL_{t-1} + MFM_t * volume_t. Over the trailing N = 40 bars, z-score the close series and the ADL series separately, then run OLS of each on the bar index 1..40. Let T_p and T_a be the t-statistics of the two slopes. SHORT entry: T_p >= +2.0 AND T_a <= -1.0 AND close_t is the highest close of the last 40 bars. LONG entry: T_p <= -2.0 AND T_a >= +1.0 AND close_t is the lowest close of the last 40 bars. Enter at the next bar's open.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit when the sign of T_a flips to agree with T_p (divergence resolved), OR at 3.0 x ATR14 target, OR at 1.5 x ATR14 stop, OR 20 bars after entry, whichever first.
inputs: rolling 40-bar OLS slope t-statistics of z-scored close and z-scored ADL
ideas.why: The A/D line weights each bar's volume by where the bar closed within its range, so a series of up-days that all close mid-range accumulates far less than the price chart suggests. When price is trending up with statistical significance while the volume-weighted flow is trending down with statistical significance, the advance is being distributed into. Using OLS t-statistics rather than peak-to-peak comparison removes the two worst problems with hand-drawn divergence: which pivots you chose, and whether the slope difference is meaningful at all given the noise.
ideas.novelty: Divergence is tested as a significance-weighted disagreement between two fitted regression slopes over a fixed window, not as a pivot-to-pivot comparison, so it is fully deterministic. And the flow series is volume-weighted by intrabar close location, which is a different construct from the momentum oscillator used by the RSI divergence already in the set.
ideas.source: Chaikin A/D line and Money Flow Multiplier formula per the Chaikin Oscillator documentation at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/dd456722(v=vs.140) and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/chaikin-oscillator/ (MFM = ((C-L)-(H-C))/(H-L), ADL = ADL_prev + MFM * volume). The OLS-t-statistic divergence test is my own construction; the sources describe divergence only qualitatively.

ideas.name: Negative And Positive Volume Index Pair
ideas.entry_rule: Initialise NVI = PVI = 1000 at the start of history. For each day: pct = close_t/close_{t-1} - 1. If volume_t < volume_{t-1}, NVI_t = NVI_{t-1} * (1 + pct) else NVI_t = NVI_{t-1}. If volume_t > volume_{t-1}, PVI_t = PVI_{t-1} * (1 + pct) else PVI_t = PVI_{t-1}. ENTRY LONG on the close of the first day where NVI_t > EMA(NVI, 255) AND PVI_t <= EMA(PVI, 255) AND that combination was not true on day t-1.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit on the close of the first day where NVI_t < EMA(NVI, 255). Secondary risk exit: a daily close more than 2.5 x ATR14 below the highest close since entry.
params: whether to require the PVI condition at all (isolates its contribution)
ideas.why: Dysart and Fosback's premise is that informed money accumulates on quiet days and uninformed money chases on loud days. NVI isolates the return earned exclusively on days when volume FELL - a return stream that discards the noisy, attention-driven sessions entirely. Requiring NVI above its long EMA while PVI is not says: the quiet-day return stream is compounding upward while the loud-day stream is not, which is the cleanest available separation of patient accumulation from crowd chasing. Fosback reported the NVI/EMA condition was strongly associated with bull markets.
ideas.novelty: The signal is built from a return series conditionally SAMPLED by the sign of the day-over-day volume change - the price series it trends on is not the actual price series at all. Nothing else in the set filters which bars contribute to the indicator based on a volume comparison, and the two-index pairing (require one above its EMA and the other below) is a joint condition on two such streams.
ideas.source: Paul Dysart's original NVI; Norman Fosback, 'Stock Market Logic' (1976), which introduced the percentage-price-change version and the one-year-EMA rule. Formulas and the 255-day EMA rule per StockCharts ChartSchool, https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/negative-volume-index-nvi , with PVI per https://guide.traderevolution.com/project/desktop-application-for-windows/desktop-application-for-mac/technical-indicators/volume/pvi-positive-volume-index . The joint NVI-up/PVI-down entry condition and the ATR exit are my specification.

ideas.name: High Volume Day Return Premium
ideas.entry_rule: Universe: all tradeable symbols with a 50-day median dollar volume of at least $2,000,000. For each symbol on day t, classify t as a HIGH-VOLUME day if volume_t is the largest of the trailing 50 trading days (t-49..t). Additional selectivity filter: the symbol's 50-day median dollar volume must be in the BOTTOM half of the universe's cross-sectional distribution that day (the effect is documented as stronger in less-visible names). BUY at the next session's open, equal dollar weight, capped at N concurrent positions per symbol of 1 and a portfolio cap of K positions (K a parameter). Repeat daily, so the book is an overlapping ladder of up to 20 entry cohorts.
ideas.exit_rule: Sell at the close of the 20th trading day after entry, unconditionally. Optional risk overlay for testing: hard stop at -15% from entry.
inputs: daily OHLCV for the whole universe
50-day median dollar volume, per symbol and cross-sectionally
params: high-volume definition: strict max vs top decile
ideas.why: Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin document that stocks with unusually high trading volume over a day or a week appreciate over the following month, and unusually low volume stocks depreciate. Their explanation is a visibility/recognition channel: a volume shock puts a stock on more screens, expands its investor base, and lowers its required return - which is a price increase. This is not an information story, so it does not require you to know what the news was, only that participation spiked.
ideas.novelty: A pure volume EVENT with a fixed calendar holding period and no price condition whatsoever - direction is not read from the bar at all. Every one of the existing 32 requires a price trigger. This one buys on abnormal attention regardless of whether the day was up or down.
ideas.source: Gervais, S., Kaniel, R. and Mingelgrin, D. (2001), 'The High-Volume Return Premium', Journal of Finance 56(3), 877-919 - https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00349 ; working-paper version at https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9901.pdf ; author page https://sites.duke.edu/sgervais/research/gervais-kaniel-mingelgrin-2001/ . Cross-country confirmation: Kaniel, Ozoguz & Starks, 'The high volume return premium: cross-country evidence', JFE 2012. The specific implementation parameters (50-day window, $2m floor, 20-day hold) are my operationalisation.

ideas.name: Momentum Life Cycle Turnover Interaction
ideas.entry_rule: Monthly, on the first trading day, for each symbol with 50-day median dollar volume >= $2,000,000 compute: MOM = close_{t-5} / close_{t-131} - 1 (roughly 6-month return skipping the last week); and RVOL_LONGRUN = mean(volume over the last 126 trading days) / mean(volume over the last 756 trading days) - a shares-outstanding-free proxy for turnover level. Sort the universe into terciles on MOM and, independently, into terciles on RVOL_LONGRUN. EARLY-STAGE LONG leg: symbols in the TOP MOM tercile AND the BOTTOM RVOL_LONGRUN tercile (low-volume winners). EARLY-STAGE SHORT leg: symbols in the BOTTOM MOM tercile AND the TOP RVOL_LONGRUN tercile (high-volume losers). Equal dollar weight each leg, entered at the next open.
ideas.exit_rule: Hold exactly 3 months (63 trading days), then close. Run three overlapping cohorts so one third of the book turns over each month. No stops in the base version; test a -20% per-name stop as a variant.
ideas.why: Lee and Swaminathan's momentum life cycle says trading volume tells you WHERE in the underreaction-to-overreaction arc a stock sits. High-turnover winners are late-stage - the crowd has already arrived, and they revert fastest. Low-turnover winners are early-stage - the move is real but under-attended, and it has further to run. The same logic inverted gives high-volume losers as the better short. Volume therefore predicts the magnitude and persistence of momentum, not just its presence, which is why the interaction beats momentum alone.
ideas.novelty: A two-way cross-sectional sort where volume determines the EXPECTED PERSISTENCE of a price signal rather than confirming or vetoing it. Volume changes how long you should hold, and which end of the momentum distribution to take, which is a genuinely different use than any confirmation filter.
ideas.source: Lee, C.M.C. and Swaminathan, B. (2000), 'Price Momentum and Trading Volume', Journal of Finance 55(5) - https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00280 ; international confirmation in 'Trading Volume and Momentum: The International Evidence', https://sites.uwasa.fi/mfjuva/wp-content/blogs.dir/4/files/sites/231/2025/02/MJ0p1a4fk7lfg1h65i61du41mm5lt14.pdf ; life-cycle revisit at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378426621000777 . PROXY NOTE: their turnover is volume/shares-outstanding, which we do not have. I substituted a within-name long-run relative volume ratio, which captures 'is this name being traded more than it usually is' but NOT the cross-sectional turnover level - test both this and a simple cross-sectional rank of log(dollar volume) as alternatives.

ideas.name: Kyle Lambda Depth Regime Entry
ideas.entry_rule: Signed volume from close location: sv_i = volume_i * (2*(close_i - low_i)/(high_i - low_i) - 1), which lies in [-volume, +volume]; use sv_i = 0 if high_i == low_i. Over a rolling window of 100 bars, fit OLS: (close_i - close_{i-1})/close_{i-1} = alpha + lambda * sv_i. Lambda is the estimated price impact per unit of signed volume. Compute L = the percentile rank of the current lambda within its own trailing 500 estimates. ENTRY LONG: L crosses from >= 20 down to < 20 (the market has just become unusually DEEP) AND the 20-bar return (close_t/close_{t-20} - 1) > 0. ENTRY SHORT: L crosses down through 20 AND the 20-bar return < 0. Enter at the next bar's open. Take no new positions while L >= 80.
ideas.exit_rule: Exit when L rises to >= 80 (the market has become thin - moves are impact, not information), OR at a 1.5 x ATR14 stop, OR 20 bars after entry, whichever first. If flat and L >= 80, stay flat.
inputs: rolling 100-bar OLS of return on signed volume
ideas.why: Kyle's lambda is the slope of price against order flow - how much the market moves per unit of net buying. When lambda is low, the book is deep: an existing trend is being sustained despite it being cheap to trade against, which means the demand is real rather than an artefact of thin liquidity. When lambda is high, the same price move could have been produced by a small order hitting an empty book, and it carries no information. Trading only in the low-lambda regime filters out precisely the moves that mean-revert once liquidity returns.
ideas.novelty: The signal is a regression COEFFICIENT between two series, tracked as a regime variable - not a level, a cross, or a divergence. It is signed (unlike Amihud) and estimated over a rolling window, so it measures directional depth. Entry timing is driven by a change in the market's impact function, with price contributing only a sign.
ideas.source: Kyle, A. (1985), 'Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading', Econometrica 53(6) - lambda as the price-impact coefficient. Estimator (OLS of price change on signed volume) as implemented in https://github.com/twowaymind/orderflow-metrics (function kyleLambda). Discussion of lambda vs low-frequency proxies in Goyenko, Holden & Trzcinka (2009). PROXY NOTE: true signed volume requires trade-level data; I use the close-location-value split described for CVD proxies at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/cumulative-volume-delta/ (buy volume = volume * (close-low)/(high-low)), which is directionally useful but not exact - this is the main modelling risk in the idea and worth testing against a tick-rule sign as an alternative.

ideas.name: Elder Force Index Pullback
ideas.entry_rule: Force Index FI_t = (close_t - close_{t-1}) * volume_t. Compute FI2 = EMA(FI, 2) and FI13 = EMA(FI, 13). ENTRY LONG on the close of day t when all hold: EMA(close, 22) at t is greater than at t-1 (medium-term uptrend intact); FI13_t > 0; FI2_t < 0 while FI2_{t-1} >= 0 (the short-horizon force just flipped negative - a pullback in flow terms); and close_t > EMA(close, 22). ENTRY SHORT is the exact mirror: EMA(close, 22) falling, FI13_t < 0, FI2 crosses from >= 0 to < 0... no - for shorts require FI2_t > 0 while FI2_{t-1} <= 0, and close_t < EMA(close, 22).
ideas.exit_rule: Exit longs when FI13 crosses below zero, OR at a stop placed at the lowest low of the last 3 bars minus 0.25 x ATR14, OR at a 3.0 x ATR14 target. Mirror for shorts. Hard time exit after 20 bars.
ideas.why: Force Index multiplies the net price change by the volume that produced it, so it measures the size of the push rather than just its direction. Elder's insight is that in an established uptrend, a brief NEGATIVE reading on the short Force Index marks a moment when selling pressure has appeared but the medium-term force is still positive - the point of maximum reward-to-risk for joining. The pullback is detected in signed-volume space, which fires at different times than a price pullback: a two-day drift down on collapsing volume produces a much shallower FI dip than a one-day drop on heavy volume, and the second is the one you want to avoid.
ideas.novelty: The pullback is measured in the signed-volume series, not the price series, so it is not an EMA-pullback reskin - a shallow price dip on huge volume triggers where a price-based rule would not, and a deep dip on no volume does not trigger where a price-based rule would. The two-speed EMA pair on the FORCE series (rather than on price) is the distinguishing construct.
ideas.source: Alexander Elder, 'Trading for a Living' (Wiley, 1993), Force Index chapter; formula and Elder's 2-period/13-period recommendation per StockCharts ChartSchool, https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/technical-indicators-and-overlays/technical-indicators/force-index , and TC2000's exact expression XAVG((C - C1) * V, 2) at https://help.tc2000.com/m/69445/l/755859-elder-force-index . The 22-EMA trend gate is Elder's own; the ATR-based exits and the explicit cross-from-nonnegative trigger are my specification to remove ambiguity.

ideas.name: Hikkake Inside-Bar Trap
ideas.entry_rule: Let A = bar[-2], R = bar[-3], B = bar[-1]. Require A is an inside bar: high(A) < high(R) AND low(A) > low(R). LONG SETUP: B breaks A downward, i.e. low(B) < low(A) AND high(B) < high(A). On the close of B, place a buy stop at high(A) + 0.01. The order stays live for exactly 3 bars after B and is cancelled if unfilled. SHORT SETUP is the mirror: high(B) > high(A) AND low(B) > low(A), place a sell stop at low(A) - 0.01, live 3 bars. No other filter; the pattern is the whole signal.
ideas.exit_rule: On fill, initial stop = the lowest low between B and the entry bar minus 0.01 (longs) / highest high plus 0.01 (shorts). Profit target = entry +/- 1.0 x (high(A) - low(B)) for longs, (high(B) - low(A)) for shorts. Hard time exit at the close of the 10th bar after entry if neither level is touched.
params: inside-bar strictness (strict > / >= on the high and low)
ideas.why: An inside bar is a public compression level; breakout traders stack stop orders just beyond it. When the first break fails and price runs back through the opposite side of the same inside bar, those breakout entries are underwater and their stops become fuel in the new direction. The edge is the trapped-order flow, which is why the confirmation window has to be short - if the reversal takes more than 3 bars the trapped positions have already been liquidated.
ideas.novelty: This is the inverse of every breakout entry we already run (Donchian, ATR expansion, squeeze release): the signal is a FAILED break of a compression bar and the entry level is the compression bar's opposite side. Unlike our liquidity-sweep rule it requires a completed bar to close beyond the level first, not just a wick.
ideas.source: Chesler, D. L., 'Trading False Moves with the Hikkake Pattern', Active Trader magazine, April 2004 (author's copy: chesler.us/resources/articles/chesler0404.pdf; mirror: oxfordstrat.com/coasdfASD32/uploads/2019/05/Trading-False-Moves.pdf). Rule confirmation from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hikkake_pattern and tradingsetupsreview.com/hikkake/ (both state the 3-period confirmation window and the stop placed at the inside bar's opposite extreme).

ideas.name: Turtle Soup (stale-extreme false breakout)
ideas.entry_rule: LONG: today's low < min(low[1..20]) - a new 20-day low - AND the bar that set that prior 20-day low occurred at least 4 trading days ago (compute the index of the prior 20-day low; require current_index - that_index >= 4). When the new low prints, place a buy stop at (prior 20-day low + 0.05), live for the remainder of today and all of the next bar. SHORT is the exact mirror at 20-day highs with a sell stop at (prior 20-day high - 0.05).
ideas.exit_rule: Initial stop = today's low - 0.05 (longs). First target = entry + 1.0 x ATR(14); take the whole position there. If the target is not reached, exit on the close of the 2nd bar after entry regardless of P/L. If the trade is profitable at that close, instead trail on the 2-bar low and exit on the first close below it.
inputs: 20-bar rolling high/low with the index of the extreme
params: minimum age of the prior extreme (4 bars)
ideas.why: A channel low that has stood untested for several days accumulates resting sell stops beneath it from trend followers and protective stops from holders. A single push through that clears them without follow-through means the selling was mechanical rather than informational; price then snaps back through the level as the liquidity vacuum closes. The age requirement is the point - a low set yesterday has not accumulated enough resting orders to make the flush meaningful.
ideas.novelty: Distinct from our liquidity-sweep rule in three concrete ways: it requires the swept extreme to be at least 4 bars old, it enters on a resting stop order AT the level rather than on a close back inside, and it carries a hard 2-bar time exit rather than a structure-based one. The recency filter alone changes the signal set substantially.
ideas.source: Connors, L. and Raschke, L. B. (1995), 'Street Smarts: High Probability Short Term Trading Strategies', the 'Turtle Soup' and 'Turtle Soup Plus One' chapters (new 20-day extreme where the previous 20-day extreme occurred at least four trading days earlier; entry via stop at the prior extreme).

ideas.name: Extreme-Bar Two-Day Reversal
ideas.entry_rule: Compute r = close/close[-1] - 1 and s = standard deviation of the last 20 daily returns. LONG when ALL hold: r <= -3.0 x s; r <= -0.05 in absolute terms; the close sits in the bottom 30% of the bar, (close - low)/(high - low) <= 0.30; and the 20-day average dollar volume (close x volume) >= $20,000,000. Buy at the next bar's open. SHORT is the mirror (r >= +3.0 x s, r >= +0.05, close in the top 30% of the bar), which the literature says is the weaker side - test it separately.
ideas.exit_rule: Pure time exit: close the position at the close of the 2nd trading day after entry. Single hard stop meanwhile at entry_bar_low - 0.5 x ATR(14) (longs). No profit target - the exit structure is deliberately time-based so the test measures the documented 2-day drift and nothing else.
ideas.why: Documented short-horizon overreaction: a one-day move of several sigma is dominated by liquidity demand (forced selling, index/ETF flow, panic) rather than by information, and the price concession paid to that demand is recovered over the next one to two sessions. The close-location filter selects for bars that ended at the extreme - i.e. where the liquidity demand was still unfilled at the bell - which is exactly the case that should snap back.
ideas.novelty: Both the trigger and the exit are unlike anything in the current set: the trigger is a return standardised by the stock's own recent volatility combined with where the close sits inside the bar, and the exit is a fixed 2-day clock with no target. The liquidity floor is deliberate - the academic reversal is largely an artefact of spread and low price in illiquid names, so the test must exclude them or it will find a fake edge.
ideas.source: Bremer, M. and Sweeney, R. J. (1991), 'The Reversal of Large Stock-Price Decreases', Journal of Finance 46(2) - stocks falling 10%+ in a day rebound roughly 2.2% over the following two days. Cox, D. R. and Peterson, D. R. (1994), 'Stock Returns following Large One-Day Declines: Evidence on Short-Term Reversals and Longer-Term Performance', Journal of Finance 49(1) (onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1994.tb04428.x) - reversal concentrated in low-price/illiquid names, hence the liquidity filter. Atkins, A. B. and Dyl, E. A. (1990), 'Price Reversals, Bid-Ask Spreads, and Market Efficiency', JFQA 25, 535-547 - reversal largely inside the spread. Zawadowski, Kertesz and Andor, 'Short-term market reaction after extreme price changes of liquid stocks' (arXiv cond-mat/0406696; Quantitative Finance) - significant reversal after BOTH intraday increases and decreases in liquid names, but NYSE spread widening eats most of it.

ideas.name: Close-Location Absorption Run
ideas.entry_rule: Define CLV_t = ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low), set to 0 when high == low. This is +1 for a close on the high, -1 for a close on the low. LONG setup when ALL hold over the last 3 completed bars: mean(CLV) >= 0.60; every individual bar has CLV >= 0.30; |close[0] - close[-3]| <= 0.25 x ATR(14) (essentially no net price progress); the sum of the 3 bars' ranges >= 2.5 x ATR(14) (the bars were not quiet); and total volume over the 3 bars >= 1.2 x 3 x the 20-bar average volume. Entry: buy stop at max(high) of those 3 bars + 0.01, valid 2 bars. SHORT is the mirror with CLV <= -0.60 / <= -0.30.
ideas.exit_rule: Initial stop = the minimum low of the 3 setup bars - 0.01. Exit immediately on any bar that closes with CLV <= -0.50 (a decisive close on the low reverses the whole premise). Otherwise trail on the 3-bar low and hard-exit at the close of the 10th bar after entry.
ideas.why: Buyers repeatedly winning the close while price goes nowhere on heavy, wide-ranging trade is the signature of a large seller being absorbed: the supply is being taken at a flat average price and the moment it is exhausted the constraint on price disappears. The two constraints together - strong closes AND no net progress - are what identify absorption rather than plain momentum.
ideas.novelty: The signal is a DIVERGENCE between where bars close and where price actually goes, which no trend, oscillator or band rule in the current set can express. Requiring near-zero net movement explicitly excludes the three-bar momentum case we already trade; a bar sequence that fires this rule would be invisible to it.
ideas.source: Synthesis. The CLV statistic is the standard close-location term from the Williams Accumulation/Distribution and Chaikin Accumulation-Distribution Line constructions; the absorption reading (strong closes with no net price change on heavy volume) is the Volume Spread Analysis interpretation from Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (1993).
